title: An embed outage opens the picked lesson at its start instead of losing it
body:
## Summary
bestWindow threw on any embedding failure, so a lesson the text model picked became "no lesson covers this one".

## Description
desk/src/lib/library/lessons.ts:102-112 (base) awaited ensureVectors() and the query embed with no guard; desk/src/lib/desk/pick.ts:44 awaits bestWindow, so the lesson job failed and desk/src/app/api/hint/route.ts:71-74 landed lesson null. The same function already opened a lesson with no vectors at its first window (lessons.ts:107 base): the failure door did not. The registry technique embedding-lifecycle ("absence is a mode, not an error") and the failure-not-empty-success law name this: an outage presented as an honest empty. Fixed: both doors return the first window with score 0 and degraded: true, and say it once in the server log.

## Flow
- Ollama down -> learner asks a maths hint -> pickLesson picks a lesson id -> bestWindow -> embed throws
- before: the lesson job fails -> TV: "no lesson covers this one"
- after: the lesson opens at its first window, marked degraded, one log line

## Expected impact
A learner whose desk has no running embedder still gets the lesson the model chose. Measured by DEGRADED-1. Could break: a consumer relying on the throw (only engines-rules-test HL4 did; strengthened).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - an engine outage no longer drops a picked lesson
Before: 2 of 2 embed failure doors (build, query) reject bestWindow
After: 0 of 2; both resolve to the first window, degraded: true, 1 log line each
Method: gate - library-rules-test DEGRADED-1 red then green; engines-rules-test HL4 strengthened
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
desk/src/lib/library/lessons.ts:104-111 (base 699112d3^):
  let all = await ensureVectors(); ... const [q] = (await embed({ texts: [query], use: "lesson-window" })).json;  // no catch
desk/src/lib/desk/pick.ts:44  const w = l.youtube ? await bestWindow(...) : null;
desk/src/app/api/hint/route.ts:74  .then((p) => { if (!p.ok) landed(null); })
DEGRADED-1 before: EngineError: ollama is not running (exit 1); after: pass

title: The host's A26-A28 no longer cite the 1MA1 specification as their source
body:
## Summary
gcse.ts stamped A26-A28, statements the host wrote and no specification holds, with the Pearson 1MA1 specification as their source.

## Description
desk/src/lib/library/gcse.ts:144 (base) mapped every statement to source: SPEC.source, while gcse.ts:82-84 says A26-A28 "are not DfE subject-content codes: the host's own additions" (a logarithm, a function's domain). The module's honest-limits header forbids claiming more than it can back; the provenance field claimed a source for content the source does not contain, and tools/gcse-coverage.cjs listed the three as "Higher tier only". Fixed: HOST_ADDED and HOST_SOURCE in gcse.ts, the test holds DfE codes to 1MA1 and host codes to a host source, and the report gives the host additions their own line.

## Flow
- read STATEMENTS[A27].source -> "Pearson Edexcel ... 1MA1 specification"
- run node ../tools/gcse-coverage.cjs -> "Higher tier only: ... A26, A27, A28"
- after: A27.source = HOST_SOURCE; the report lists them as host additions

## Expected impact
Whoever verifies the map (VERIFIED=false until a person checks every line against SPEC.source) is no longer sent to the specification for three lines it does not contain. No screen reads .source.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - provenance names only what the source holds
Before: host additions citing 1MA1: 3 of 3; listed as higher tier: 3
After: 0 of 3; listed apart: 3
Method: gate - gcse-rules-test red at A26 before, green after
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
desk/src/lib/library/gcse.ts:82-87 comment "A26-A28 are not DfE subject-content codes: the host's own additions"
desk/src/lib/library/gcse.ts:144 (base) ].map((x) => ({ ...x, source: SPEC.source }))
tools/gcse-rules-test.cjs:20 (base) assert.match(st.source, /1MA1/) for every statement
gcse-coverage (base): "Higher tier only (not mapped): A13, A15, A16, A20, A26, A27, A28, ..."

title: The GCSE completeness test names the A1-28 it asserts, not A1-25
body:
## Summary
tools/gcse-rules-test.cjs titled its first test "A1-25" while asserting A: 28.

## Description
tools/gcse-rules-test.cjs:14 (base) "the subject content is complete: N1-16, A1-25, ..." and :15 want = { ..., A: 28, ... }. A red run would point at a count the test no longer checks. Fixed the title.

## Flow
- read the test list -> "A1-25"
- read the assertion -> A: 28
- after: the title says A1-28 and names A26-28 as the host additions

## Expected impact
A reader of a red run sees the rule the test holds. Nothing can break: a title.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a test says what it checks
Before: titles disagreeing with their assertion: 1
After: 0
Method: gate - gcse-rules-test 0 both sides; the figure is the title-vs-assert count
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
tools/gcse-rules-test.cjs:14 test('the subject content is complete: N1-16, A1-25, R1-16, ...')
tools/gcse-rules-test.cjs:15 const want = { N: 16, A: 28, R: 16, G: 25, P: 9, S: 6 };

title: gcse-coverage loads desk TypeScript through ts-load, the suites' one loader
body:
## Summary
tools/gcse-coverage.cjs carried a private copy of the TypeScript loader that tools/ts-load.cjs calls "the one loader".

## Description
tools/gcse-coverage.cjs:5-10 (base) patched Module._resolveFilename and require.extensions itself, uncached, with a bare require of desk/node_modules/typescript (a stack trace where ts-load prints "npm install in desk/ first"). tools/ts-load.cjs:1-12 is the shared loader with the alias, hooks and a transpile cache. Fixed: one require of ts-load.

## Flow
- node ../tools/gcse-coverage.cjs from desk/ -> private loader, ~300 ms
- after: ts-load, ~85 ms, same bytes

## Expected impact
One loader to change when the TS options move; the report runs 3.5x faster. Could break: nothing seen; output cmp-identical from desk/ and root.

## Evaluation
Claim: other - one loader instead of two
Before: 6 private loader lines; 284-328 ms a run (3 runs)
After: 1 require; 79-89 ms a run (3 runs); output byte-identical
Method: probe - timed runs and cmp of the output; no suite runs the report
Result: better
Gate: none

title: A VTT NOTE, STYLE or REGION block is no longer read as caption text
body:
## Summary
parseVtt skipped only the header line of a NOTE block, so the comment lines under it were appended to the previous cue.

## Description
desk/src/lib/library/vtt.ts:19 (base) dropped a line starting with NOTE but not the block that follows it up to the blank line, as WebVTT defines; STYLE and REGION blocks had no rule at all. The appended text goes into the 40-second window that is embedded and shown as the seek caption. VTT-2 and VTT-3 already made the reader follow WebVTT for identifiers and hour-less timings. Fixed: a NOTE/STYLE/REGION block after a blank line is skipped to the next blank line.

## Flow
- a transcript with "NOTE checked by hand" over two lines between cues
- before: the previous cue reads "first line by hand in October"
- after: "first line"

## Expected impact
Retrieval embeds what was said, not the transcript author's notes. YouTube captions (no blocks) parse identically, so no vector digest moves.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - only caption text is indexed
Before: VTT-4 fixture: 2 of 3 cues carry comment text
After: 0 of 3
Method: gate - library-rules-test VTT-4 red then green; VTT-1..3 still green
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
desk/src/lib/library/vtt.ts:19 (base) if (/^(WEBVTT|Kind:|Language:|NOTE)/.test(ln)) { ... continue; }  // the header line only
VTT-4 before: text: "first line by hand in October", "second line a comment on two lines of its own"

title: A transcript replaced while the desk runs is read and embedded again
body:
## Summary
lessonWindows cached windows by id for the process, so a re-fetched transcript was never read until a restart.

## Description
desk/src/lib/library/lessons.ts:21-22 (base) returned the cached windows for any id once read, and bestWindow rebuilt vectors only for a lesson missing from the map (lessons.ts:106 base). The sibling case, a transcript ADDED while running, was fixed in bd80b766; a REPLACED one was not, though the vector cache's digest already keys on window text. Fixed: the window cache holds the file's size and mtime; the published vector map remembers each lesson's window digest and a mismatch rebuilds once.

## Flow
- a lesson picked with old captions
- captions fetched again (new mtime)
- before: old text, seek on old vectors; after: new windows, re-embedded, seek lands in them

## Expected impact
An operator who corrects a transcript sees it on the next pick. Cost: one statSync per lookup.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the seek uses the transcript on disk
Before: LATE-2: old text returned, seek at 0:00 on stale vectors
After: new two windows, seek at 0:50
Method: gate - library-rules-test LATE-2 red on the base file, green after
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
desk/src/lib/library/lessons.ts:21 (base) if (cache.has(id)) return cache.get(id)!;
desk/src/lib/library/lessons.ts:106 (base) if (!all.has(lessonId) && ...) rebuild  // presence only, not content

title: A lesson with no transcript on disk is said once in the server log
body:
## Summary
A missing transcript made every pick of that lesson open at 0:00 with no caption, and nothing named the missing file.

## Description
desk/src/lib/library/lessons.ts:25 (base) returned [] for a missing <data>/lessons/<id>.en.vtt with no signal. Transcripts are local-only (lessons.ts:13), so on a fresh machine every maths lesson degrades silently. grep "en.vtt" over desk/src, tools, scripts: one reader, no status. Fixed: one log line per lesson per process with the path; a transcript placed later is still read.

## Flow
- fresh machine, no <data>/lessons
- pick a maths lesson -> opens at 0:00, no caption
- after: the server log names the file it looked for

## Expected impact
The operator learns which transcripts to fetch. Could break: nothing; one console line.

## Evaluation
Claim: other - a silent degraded mode is said
Before: log lines naming a missing transcript: 0
After: 1 per lesson per process
Method: gate - library-rules-test MISSING-1 red on the base file, green after
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
desk/src/lib/library/lessons.ts:25 (base) if (!existsSync(f)) return [];
grep -rn "en\.vtt" desk/src tools scripts -> lessons.ts:24 and test fixtures only

title: pickLesson drops bestWindow's degraded mark before the TV
body:
## Summary
bestWindow now marks an embed-outage seek degraded, but desk/src/lib/desk/pick.ts copies only t and text into the LessonPick.

## Description
desk/src/lib/desk/pick.ts:45 builds { id, title, t, text, why, youtube } from the window; the degraded flag (lessons.ts bestWindow, 699112d3) is lost, and the LessonPick type in desk/src/lib/session/store.ts has no field for it. relevance-floors: a degraded slice must say so, or the consumer prices it as the full answer; the TV keeps claiming the lesson starts at the part that matters. Fix: carry degraded on LessonPick and let the lesson screen say "from the start" in the caption slot.

## Flow
- embedder down -> pick -> bestWindow degraded
- pick.ts copies t/text only
- TV: the lesson at 0:00 presented as the chosen part

## Expected impact
The learner is told the lesson opens from the start, not at the part that matters. Could break: the store type and a TV screen (On Air caption).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a degraded seek is labelled where it is shown
Before: degraded marks reaching LessonPick: 0 of 1
After: predicted 1 of 1
Method: simulation - pick.ts, store.ts and the TV screen are outside this round's paths (desk-pipelines, session, tv)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: desk/src/lib/desk/pick.ts:45 return { id: l.id, title: l.title, t: w?.t ?? 0, text: w?.text ?? "", why: ..., youtube: l.youtube };
instrument: a pick test stubbing embed to throw: assert LessonPick.degraded === true and the lesson screen render (server-side) carries the from-the-start caption; seed red by dropping the field

title: A cold vector cache embeds the lessons in one engine call each, serially
body:
## Summary
build() calls the embedding engine once per lesson in a loop, so the first pick on a cold cache waits for eight serial calls.

## Description
desk/src/lib/library/lessons.ts build() loops LESSONS with youtube (8) and awaits embed({ texts: w }) per lesson; the first pick after a model change or a fresh data dir pays every call before the seek. One call with every window (or a bounded batch) would cut it, but Ollama's /api/embed batch size and memory on the operator's box are unmeasured here.

## Flow
- fresh DESK_DATA_DIR or new OLLAMA_EMBED_MODEL
- first maths pick -> ensureVectors -> 8 serial embed calls
- proposal: batch all windows into one (or N) calls, split the answer by lesson

## Expected impact
The first pick after a cold start is faster. Could break: a batch over the engine's limit fails the whole build (now a degraded seek, not a lost lesson).

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - fewer engine round trips on a cold cache
Before: 8 embed calls per cold build (counted from the loop)
After: predicted 1 (or ceil(windows/batch))
Method: simulation - the stub counts calls but cannot price Ollama latency or its batch limit
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: desk/src/lib/library/lessons.ts build(): for (const l of LESSONS.filter((l) => l.youtube)) { ... const { json } = await embed({ texts: w.map((x) => x.text), use: "lesson-window" }); ... }
instrument: a stub counting embed calls on a cold cache (8 -> 1) plus one timed live cold build on the operator's Ollama, both arms
